newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDIC investigating LippoBank dealings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDIC investigating LippoBank dealings.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. has launched an internal investigation to determine whether it's supervision over a bank owned by Indonesian financier James Riady was compromised, according to a published report on Sunday.

In particular, the agency is trying to learn why a high- level supervisor at the agency met with John Huang, a Commerce Department official and former top executive at Riady's LippoBank, the Los Angeles Times reported.
The FDIC has twice within the past six year issued, then lifted sanctions against LippoBank for improper practices, the newspaper said.

LippoBank, which is 98.7 percent owned by Riady's family, first came under scrutiny because of the family's connections to President Bill Clinton and the recent disclosure of large campaign donations by Indonesian interests to the Democratic Party.

Huang, who left his Commerce Department job to become a fund-raiser for the Democratic Party, has been at the centre of a controversy over alleged mixing of private interests, government policy and political donations.
On Saturday, the New York Times reported Clinton twice discussed policy about Indonesia and China with Riady but the discussions never influenced policy decisions.

According to the Los Angeles Times, message slips obtained by the Commerce Department show that FDIC executive Ken Quincy telephoned Huang twice in May of 1995 and scheduled a meeting with him in the regulator's office.

At the time, LippoBank was under a "cease-and-desist" order from the FDIC and was seeking return to normal status. Quincy approved the lifting of that sanction last March, the Los Angeles Times reported.
The bank's president and chief executive officer, James Per Lee, told the paper that no one has exerted influence to help the insitution.
"They (FDIC officials) have never done us any favours," he said. "Everything has been a struggle."

Robert Garsson, a spokesman for the FDIC, told the daily that the FDIC has no reason to believe that LippoBank has received preferential treatment, but said the agency was looking into the reason for the meeting with Huang.
He also said Quincy told officials he has no recollection of calling or meeting Huang last year.

"We don't know what the situation is there," Garsson said. "I don't think a receptionist (at the Commerce Department) would put it down out of thin air. Frankly, we have no explanation for that just now."
